suggestions.rationale: Clinical Mapping Master Batch 2026 publishes this relationship only as rare infection complication. Require documented Actinomyces infection and separately diagnosed infective endocarditis attributable to Actinomyces; do not infer cardiac disease from actinomycosis alone. Evidence is a systematic review of rare reported Actinomyces endocarditis cases; frequency and individual attribution are uncertain. The cited literature supports only this bounded proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-11 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Actinomycotic osteomyelitis is a rare chronic infection caused by Actinomyces species; mandibular involvement can occur in cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis. Require clinically established cervicofacial/oral actinomycosis plus a separately diagnosed mandibular osteomyelitis phenotype. Do not generalize to all actinomycosis or all osteomyelitis. Preserve odontogenic infection, trauma, surgery, malignancy and other infectious causes. The source is rare-disease/case-plus-review evidence and must not be presented as population-level causal proof. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
